To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have developed a novel method for estimating derivatives from noisy data that uses a truncated Jacobi series expansion, (2) we have analyzed the noise contribution to this estimation method, and (3) we have shown that the proposed method has a lower noise contribution than other derivative estimators.
the Jacobi derivative estimations are robust to noise and that their statistical properties are well known.

we have shown how to extend the algebraic differentiation methods of Mboup et al., 2007, 2009 to a more general setting by using a truncated Jacobi series expansion, and we have provided a detailed error analysis of the noise error contribution in the case of stochastic process noise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the noise error in Jacobi derivative estimations.
the estimation of a derivative of a function from its noisy observation signal and with the study of the noise error contribution.
the estimation of the derivatives of a function from noisy observations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Jacobi derivative estimator is an efficient method to estimate the derivatives of a noisy observation, and it has a good performance in terms of accuracy. Moreover
the derivative estimation is more robust with respect to the noise level if the parameter α is close to −1.
, under the assumptions made in this paper, the proposed method is the most accurate method in the sense of minimizing the mean square error.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the existence of a derivative estimator of a signal with noise, which is a truncated Jacobi series expansion of the iterated integral (of the observation signal).
the Jacobi derivative estimator is the best one in terms of the noise error contribution.

, by using a truncated Jacobi series expansion of the noisy observation signal, we obtain a derivative estimation which is more robust than the classical derivative estimation obtained by using only the first two integrals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown how the noise error contribution can be reduced by a judicious choice of the parameters in the truncated Jacobi orthogonal expansions.
the derivative estimators can be used in a variety of settings.
we provide a new approach to estimate derivatives of signals from noisy measurements.
